spans.text: Now let's lay down the basic principles that guide us in that mission (whether we understand them all as yet—or not!).
נכון לקבל עליו מצות עשה של ואהבת לרעך כמוך:

מַה טֹּבוּ (Thanks to our Torah and our mission)—our homes and our shuls are solid and good (and we can connect to Hashem anywhere). וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבֹא בֵיתֶךָ—I come to Your House to thank You for all Your kindness; and I daven to You with awe. Hashem (You created the unique me), and I come to Your holy place with love (not as a burden) and willingly submit myself to Your Will. וַאֲנִי תְפִילָתִי—May my tefillos be favorable to You. Hashem Who takes care of us, please answer my requests with Your kindness (even though I am not always deserving)—because only Your help can be relied upon.

אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם—You are the Master of the universe, Who ruled even before anything was created and will rule after all ceases to exist; and now that there IS a creation, You are proclaimed as King by all creatures: Hashem always was, is, and always will be. There is no power but You, without beginning or end, all power is Yours. (Though understanding the essence of Hashem is beyond comprehension, nevertheless, I have a unique and close relationship with Him!) He is my God; my living redeemer; He is a rock for me when I am in pain or in time of distress; He is a refuge for me; He answers me when I call to Him. (Therefore,) I entrust my spirit into His Hand when I sleep and when I am awake (I am in His Hands at all times). With my spirit, my body, Hashem is with me and therefore I fear nothing.

(The Thirteen Principles of Faith) (1) There exists a perfect God Who created everything. (2) God is One—there is only one God. (3) God cannot be viewed in bodily terms. (4) God is Eternal. (5) Jews pray directly to God with no intermediaries. (6) The prophets are true. (7) Moshe was the greatest prophet. (8) The entire Torah was given to Moshe. (9) The Torah is eternal and unchanging. (10) God knows what we do. (11) God rewards and punishes according to our actions. (12) Mashiach will come. (13) There will be Techiyas Hameisim.
Thank You, for You give us the ability to understand the difference between day and night—meaning: good and bad, right and wrong.
Thank You, for You did not create me a member of another nation (who have to go through an entire process if they want to join the Chosen People. I was given that as a gift at birth—thank You!).
Thank You, for You did not create me a servant (rather, I am free to make my own choices, be held responsible for them, and thus earn reward—thank You!).
Thank You, for You created me according to Your will (and thus I have a unique and crucial role to play, even though at times it seems unclear).
Thank You, for You did not create me a woman (and I am happy to have all those extra mitzvos!).
Thank You, for You open the eyes of the blind (and thus I am asking You to remove my blindness to the spiritual world).
Thank You, for You provide clothing for the naked (we worry about the label and style—but we need to be happy that we have clothes to wear!).

מַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים—Thank You, for You free those imprisoned ((1) imprisoned in our bodies while sleeping, with no control over our actions and thoughts—by You waking us up we now have the ability to move about and make choices—thank You; (2) imprisoned in physical prisons; or (3) imprisoned in the "prisons" we create for ourselves by our own insecurities).

זוֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים—Thank You, for You give those who are bent over (whether because of physical issues or from the difficulties and hardships in their lives) the ability to stand up straight (and deal with their struggles).
רוֹקַע הָאָרֶץ עַל הַמַּיִם—Thank You, for You establish solid ground over the waters of the deep (so we have "solid ground" upon which to build our lives).

שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי כָּל צְרָכִּי—Thank You, for You have provided me with all my needs (whatever You have given me must be what I need—not more and not less—even though sometimes that is hard to understand).

Thank You, for You (1) direct our steps; and (2) support every step we choose to take. (Sometimes You set our path and direct us into certain circumstances that are growth opportunities for us, in order to help us fulfill our ultimate mission—thank You! And when we make our own free will choice/step when responding to those circumstances, You support and allow us to make those steps, for better or worse—thank You!)
Thank You, for You give us courage and strength (to utilize our talents for the good).
Thank You, for You crown Bnei Yisrael with glory (by giving us the tools to give meaning and beauty to our lives).
Thank You, for You give strength and energy to those of us who are either physically, emotionally, or spiritually exhausted (so that we can keep going and make it through another day).
Thank You, for You woke me up physically and spiritually (for the purpose of sending me out into the world to fulfill the task You assigned to me).
Now that I'm awake, with all the gifts and tools You have given me, I ask for help to conduct myself in a way that allows me to serve You to the utmost.

May it be Your will, Hashem—Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout history—that You make Torah study something comfortable and familiar to us; and make us feel a closeness and attachment to Your mitzvos. Do not bring us into situations and challenges that could lead us to sin or to be disappointed with ourselves; and do not allow the yetzer hara to get the better of us. Keep us far away from evil people and bad friends; and help us attach ourselves to our yetzer tov and to good friends.
Compel our creative powers to be used to serve You. And may we always find favor in Your eyes, and in the eyes of everyone we meet. And do for us good acts of kindness.
You, Hashem, are the Source of everything; הַגּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל—Who does good acts of kindness to His nation, Bnei Yisrael.

May it be Your will, Hashem—Who controls everything and has taken care of Bnei Yisrael throughout history—that You protect me today and every day from arrogant and overbearing people (and from being like that myself!). Keep evil people, bad friends, and evil neighbors far away from me. (And may my dealings with people not impede my spiritual growth.)

The Akeidah is a wonderful example of getting up early and setting out to do what Hashem commanded—even though we don't understand it. We daven that the zechus of the Akeidah should help us in any difficulties that will come up during the day.
We proclaim to ourselves and the world our loyalty to Hashem. (And in case the time for the Shema will pass soon, we say it now to ensure we have said it in the proper time.)
We declare that Hashem is Eternal, and request that everyone should see the truth.

Though we will be spending the day taking care of our personal needs, we declare that we long for the time when all Jews will return to Eretz Yisrael, the Beis Hamikdash will be rebuilt, and the world will recognize the truth. And this leads into the recitation of Korbanos.

This section of davening is basically an overview of the daily avodah in the Beis Hamikdash, and of all korbanos. We say this to show that we understand that our tefillos are merely a substitute for the real service of Hashem, which was in the Beis Hamikdash with korbanos. We express our hope that we will soon have the opportunity to do that again!

• One reason is that ישמעאל (as in "רבי ישמעאל אומר") means "Hashem will hear." As we now begin the core of Shacharis, we need to reinforce in ourselves that Hashem DOES hear our tefillos, even though there are times in our lives when it seems to us that He does not.

• According to Kabbalah, the Thirteen Middos of Torah interpretation, as set down by Rabbi Yishmael, are parallel to the Thirteen Middos Ha'rachamim (Hashem, Hashem, Kel Rachum…) of Hashem. By us committing ourselves to studying Torah and applying it to our lives, Hashem will deal with us today, and always, based on His middah of Mercy and Forgiveness, rather than His middah of Strict Judgment.
FAQ: Thank you? For what? My life stinks!
ANSWER: Good point! See Appendix 2

Instant Insight: Literally, שכוי could be translated as a rooster. The uniqueness of the rooster is that it starts to crow right before the light of dawn. Night/darkness represents a lack of clarity and a sense of hopelessness. In the morning light, we see that all is really not so bad. The rooster teaches us that even in the darkest time of night, we can see the light if we use the "ability to understand" that Hashem gave us! We thank Him for that ability.
Chosen People? Doesn't this brachah sound racist? I mean, I know a lot of really nice non-Jews—and some "not-so-great" Jews! Is there really such a difference?
Common misconception! See Appendix 4.
For women:
For men:
This is not simply a FAQ—it is the FAQ. Is it so bad to be a woman that men thank Hashem that "You did not create me a woman"? And were men not created "according to Your will"?!

Crucial question! The complexity of these two brachos touch on the understanding of each person's role as a contributing member of this great mission to the world called Am Yisrael. See Appendix 11—but read it all and read it slowly.
FAQ: But I can't "stand up straight"! I've tried, but I keep falling back down. All the stuff in my life is crushing me! ANSWER: OY! Difficult question! See Appendix 3.
FAQ: If that is true, then why should we ask Hashem for stuff? עשה לי כל צרכי—He gave me all I need! ANSWER: Good thinking! See Appendix 1.

Instant Insight: This brachah is in the singular—specifically about me (gave me all my needs), unlike so many other brachos. Why? Because I need to feel satisfied with what I have. But regarding others, my job is not to tell them, "Don't worry—you have all you need," but to go help them!

Instant Insight: This brachah can also be understood in the following manner: שֶׁעָשָׂה לִי כָּל צְרָכִּי—all the "stuff" in life that You have "given" to me, all the things that I am going through, as difficult as they may seem, I believe they are all צְרָכִּי—things that I need to deal with in order to be the best "me" I can be (even if now I cannot see how). Thank You!
FAQ: Which "steps" does Hashem decide and set for us, and which do we choose on our own?
ANSWER: That is a complex issue! See Appendix 5.
Do not answer Amen after this brachah, as it is one long brachah until the words עמו ישראל.

FAQ: We say, "Do not allow the yetzer hara to get the better of us," and "Compel our creative powers to be used to serve You." But I thought we had free will? This sounds like we are asking Hashem to eliminate our free will choices!
ANSWER: Great question! See Appendix 6.

FAQ: "Do for us good acts of kindness"—What does that mean? Are there "bad" acts of kindness?
ANSWER: Clever thinking! See Appendix 7.
Some say all, some say some, some say none
We request the courage to stand up for what is right and be proud to publicly follow Torah and mitzvos.
בלחש.

FAQ:
Really? Am I supposed to wake up each morning and say to myself: "I sooo wish I could go bring an animal sacrifice this morning"? How are we supposed to relate to a concept that seems so foreign to us?
ANSWER:
Valid question! See Appendix 9.
בָּרוּךְ, שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ, לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד:
יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ, יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ, אִם נִתְחַיַּבְתִּי אָשָׁם שֶׁתְּהֵא אֲמִירָה זוּ מְרֻצָּה לְפָנֶיךָ כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּי אָשָׁם:
יְהִי רָצוֹן כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּי תּוֹדָה:
יְהִי רָצוֹן כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּי שְׁלָמִים:
Why conclude with this particular Beraisa?
